task.description: REWORK ITERATION 1: SECURITY-REVIEWER FAILed on INV-8 (handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-02c-security-reviewer.json). validate_metadata/1 in lib/letflow/event_store.ex (~line 233) RAISES instead of returning a typed {:error, _} on realistic malformed attrs[:metadata] input: an empty string or integer raises Protocol.UndefinedError; a non-tuple list or an atom-keyed map (e.g. %{foo: "bar"} -- an easy mistake since every other attrs key in this module is an atom) raises FunctionClauseError inside String.length/1. append/2's own @spec promises {:ok, _} | {:error, _} -- a raised exception on caller-controlled input violates that contract. Fix validate_metadata/1 (and audit the rest of the pre-transaction validation phase, P0-P6, for the same class of bug -- guard on is_map/1, is_binary/1, is_list/1 etc. before calling functions like String.length/1/Enum.count/1 that assume a specific shape) so every realistic malformed-attrs shape returns a typed {:error, {:invalid_metadata, _}}-shaped tuple (or whatever the design's error taxonomy already names) rather than raising. Add a regression check yourself (throwaway iex/mix run, not part of your committed artifacts) confirming at least: metadata as a non-map, metadata as an atom-keyed map, and metadata as a string, all now return {:error, _} rather than raising. Implement lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md's design: a new lib/letflow/event_store.ex context module (Letflow.EventStore) with append/2, per the design's Section 6 algorithm (now prose, not code -- your job is to turn that prose into real, correct Elixir/Ecto). Also add Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (the reverse of schema_name_for_tenant/1) to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, per the design's Section 4. No new migrations needed -- REQ-023 already created every table this touches. The design's OQ-5 (instance_projections insert-if-absent at first append) needs REVIEWER's explicit confirmation at Step 2d -- implement per the design's stated resolution but flag it again in your own handoff so it isn't missed.
acceptance_criteria: appending to a terminated instance (status CANCELLED or COMPLETED in instance_projections) returns an error and writes zero rows across all five involved tables, demonstrated by an actual test or iex session against a real Postgres, not just described

two concurrent appends to the same instance_id never receive the same sequence_number -- demonstrated with an actual concurrent test (e.g. Task.async_stream racing two appends) or, if concurrency can't be exercised in this environment, the FOR UPDATE-equivalent locking code path is cited explicitly
appending twice with the same idempotency_key returns is_duplicate: true on the second call and does not insert a second events row, verified against the idempotency sidecar table REQ-023 defines
a payload that fails REQ-024's validate_payload/2 results in zero rows written to events, instance_sequence, or instance_projections -- no partial state
a payload over 4096 bytes is split into events.payload's $ref pointer form plus an event_payload_store row, verified by reading both rows back after append

every row append/1(2) writes (events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, the idempotency sidecar) has tenant_id equal to the tenant whose schema the write targeted, derived internally -- not equal to a caller-supplied tenant_id when the two are deliberately made to disagree in a test, which must fail loudly (not silently attribute to the wrong tenant) rather than succeed

result.summary:
REWORK ITERATION 1 fix for SECURITY-REVIEWER's INV-8 FAIL (step-02c, first submission). Root cause: `validate_metadata/1` had no leading shape guard -- `map_size(metadata)` on a non-map silently fails BEAM guard evaluation and falls through to the second clause, which then calls `Enum.find_value/3`/`String.length/1` on values that were never proven to be maps or binaries, raising `Protocol.UndefinedError` (metadata `""` or `5`) or `FunctionClauseError` (metadata `[1,2,3]`/`["a","b"]` -- non-2-tuple list elements; metadata `%{foo: "bar"}` -- atom key handed to `String.length/1`).

Fix: added `defp validate_metadata(metadata) when not is_map(metadata), do: {:error, {:invalid_metadata, :not_a_map}}` as the new leading clause (catches strings/integers/lists/anything non-map before `map_size` ever runs), plus a `not is_binary(key) -> {:error, {:invalid_metadata, {:non_string_key, key}}}` cond branch inside the per-entry validator (catches atom-keyed and other non-string-keyed maps before `String.length(key)` runs). Once metadata is proven to be a map, `Enum.find_value`'s `fn {key, value} -> ...}` clause can never crash -- Elixir maps always enumerate as 2-tuples, so no separate list-element guard was needed once non-maps are rejected up front. Extended `@type metadata_violation` with `:not_a_map` and `{:non_string_key, key :: term()}`, and `@type append_error` already covered these via the existing `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, metadata_violation()}}` member -- no new top-level error variant needed for this part.

Audited the rest of P0-P6 for the same class of bug per the rework brief's explicit ask (not just the one bug already caught): `reject_tenant_id/1` (Map.has_key?, safe on any map), `fetch_uuid/3` (instance_id/actor_id -- delegates to `Ecto.UUID.cast/1`, empirically confirmed safe for every non-UUID shape: integer/atom/map/list/nil all return `:error`, never raise), `fetch_payload/1` and `fetch_idempotency_key/1` (both already gate on `is_binary/1` before any length/byte_size call -- no bug there, matching the rework brief's own rhetorical examples). Found one more real instance of the same bug class beyond metadata, not previously flagged: `event_type` was read via a bare `Map.get(attrs, :event_type)` with zero shape check, then passed straight into `Registry.validate_payload/3` (P4) which forwards it into `Registry.get_type/2`'s `where([e], e.name == ^event_type)` Ecto query -- confirmed empirically that `event_type: nil` raises `ArgumentError` ('comparing e.name with nil is forbidden'), and `event_type: :an_atom` / `event_type: 123` both raise `Ecto.Query.CastError`. This happens at P4, strictly before the `Multi`/M4 ever opens -- the design doc's own OQ-4 note (§9) says a malformed `event_type` is deliberately left to surface via `Event.insert_changeset/2`'s changeset validation at M4, but that deferral is unreachable for non-binary values: P4 crashes first. Fixed within this handoff's owned module (event_store.ex only, did not touch registry.ex) by adding `fetch_event_type/1` (same is_binary/non-empty pattern as `fetch_payload/1`) into the pre-transaction `with` chain, right after the idempotency_key checks and before metadata validation, matching the design's own stated P2 field order; added `{:error, :missing_event_type}` to `@type append_error`, symmetric with `:missing_instance_id`/`:missing_actor_id`/`:missing_payload`. Documented as a deliberate, reasoned divergence from OQ-4's literal text (with the empirical evidence cited) directly above `fetch_event_type/1`'s definition, and flagged again below for REVIEWER -- not a silent re-decision.

Verification actually run (not predicted): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` exits 0 (clean, no warnings). `mix format --check-formatted` exits 0. `mix test` -- 401 tests, 4 properties, 0 failures, full suite still green (identical count to before this fix; event_store_test.exs still doesn't exist yet, owned by TEST-DESIGNER next). Regression check: threw together `tmp_req025_regression.exs` (deleted after use, never committed), ran via `MIX_ENV=dev mix run` against the real docker-compose Postgres (port 5462), provisioning a fresh tenant schema, replaying migrations, and registering a real event type, then calling `Letflow.EventStore.append/2` directly. Actual observed return values: metadata `""` -> `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, :not_a_map}}`; metadata `5` -> `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, :not_a_map}}`; metadata `%{foo: "bar"}` -> `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, {:non_string_key, :foo}}}`; metadata `[1,2,3]` -> `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, :not_a_map}}`; metadata `["a","b"]` -> `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, :not_a_map}}`; event_type `nil` -> `{:error, :missing_event_type}`; event_type `:an_atom` -> `{:error, :missing_event_type}`; event_type `123` -> `{:error, :missing_event_type}`; a control call with valid metadata (`%{"k" => "v"}`) still returned `{:ok, %{event: %Event{...}, is_duplicate: false, ...}}` with the row actually committed -- confirming the fix doesn't reject well-formed input. Zero `RAISED` lines in the captured output (grep-confirmed) across all cases. Zero rows were written for any of the error cases (all rejected before `Repo.transaction/2` opens, per P0-P6's design).
issues: OQ-5 (design doc §9, carried over from the original submission, still unresolved): instance_projections insert-if-absent at first append (M6's upsert) is a real scope-boundary judgment call per the design's own framing, implemented exactly as designed -- needs REVIEWER's explicit confirmation at Step 2d, not just SECURITY-REVIEWER's tenant-isolation check.

OQ-1 (design doc §9, carried over): REQ-025's own acceptance criterion 6 names instance_sequence and event_idempotency as tables needing a correctly-derived tenant_id, but neither table carries a tenant_id column in REQ-023's shipped schema -- restated in Letflow.EventStore's moduledoc per the design's instruction; TEST-DESIGNER will need to adapt that acceptance criterion's test to a prefix-reachability check for those two tables rather than a column-value check.

NEW -- OQ-4 (design doc §9) is disproven by this rework's own empirical finding: the design assumed a malformed event_type would surface via M4's Event.insert_changeset/2 changeset, but P4 (Registry.validate_payload/3, which runs before the Multi/M4 ever opens) crashes first on any non-binary event_type (nil -> ArgumentError, atom/integer -> Ecto.Query.CastError). Fixed here by adding a structural fetch_event_type/1 check in event_store.ex's own pre-transaction phase (this handoff's owned module) rather than touching registry.ex (REQ-024's, not owned here). REVIEWER should confirm this divergence from OQ-4's literal text at Step 2d -- documented inline above fetch_event_type/1's definition with the empirical evidence, not silently decided.
